Bull case for funding pitch 12 (alpha-pm, K-universe 20-day momentum, top-5, 5-day rebalance).
1) The hypothesis is one of the most replicated effects in equities: recent relative winners tend to keep outperforming over short horizons. The rule is simple, with few parameters, so overfitting risk is low.
2) All gates pass: IC 0.57 (t 22.6, 720 predictions, 36 rebalances), deflated Sharpe at its cap, capacity about $4.4bn against a $1m bar, max drawdown -0.76%. Bear is right that the IC is implausibly high. That argues for a small seed and a fresh-window check, not a rejection of the mechanism.
3) K03 news is after the window end (2024-09-26), so the backtest cannot show how the book handles a gap. That is a real risk. It is managed by sizing and a stop-loss rule in the live book, not by discarding the signal. A 20-day momentum book holding a short-seller target will be hurt, but only in the names that run up into bad news.
4) Turnover 11.4 is a cost question, not a fatal flaw. With $200k seed and top-5 equal weight, I'd ask for costs at 10-20bp per trade. Even at a fraction of gross, the edge must be large to be eaten.
Recommendation: fund at a reduced seed, with out-of-sample tracking (the post-2024-09-26 window) and a cost-adjusted review at 30 days.

Bull case for funding pitch 14 (beta-pm, L-universe 20-day momentum, top-5).
1) The same hypothesis as pitch 12 and 16 is only redundant if the universes overlap. They do not: K, L and T are separate names, and correlation to pod 1 is 0.04, measured against the live pod. Three independent universes running the same simple rule is a test of the mechanism across more samples, not triple-counting.
2) Gates pass: IC 0.37 (t 10.3), Sharpe 14.8, capacity $610m against a $1m bar, correlation 0.04 against pod 1. Bear is right that the IC is far above any credible prior. The fix is an out-of-sample window, which this pitch can get for free by running live.
3) Turnover 19.4 is the highest of the three. That is the real concern, and it is a cost question. The fund should require a net-of-cost return before scaling, but the signal can start at a small seed.
4) "No L-news in three days" is not a negative. It is a quiet universe, and a quiet universe is a fair test of the signal on ordinary days, which is most days.
Recommendation: fund at the minimum seed, require cost-adjusted tracking over the next 30 trading days, and extend the window beyond 2024-03 before any scale-up.

Bull case for funding pitch 16 (gamma-pm, T-universe 20-day momentum, top-5).
1) Best correlation profile in the batch: -0.011 to pod 2 and -0.015 to pod 1. If the signal is real, this adds an independent return stream. That is exactly what a multi-pod fund needs.
2) Gates pass: IC 0.54 (t 20.2), Sharpe 26.6, max drawdown -0.67%, capacity $4.6bn. Bear's point that the numbers are implausible is fair. 3) Turnover 12.6 is a cost concern. Require a net-of-cost figure before scaling, and use a small seed while it is tested.
4) No T-news in three days is a neutral fact. The rule's risk of event gaps is real for any momentum book; sizing limits handle that.
Recommendation: fund at the minimum seed with a 30-day cost-adjusted review and a fresh-window out-of-sample test. Scale only if the net result survives.
